title: SceneEvidenceTimeline
description: Generator input for the scene-evidence production lane (doc 29 Part 8). One episode's worth of scenes; each scene is a ken-burns world plate plus up to two evidence builds with sequenced stat badges, closed by a directional wipe. The renderer derives every visual state from this document — no per-episode motion authoring. Badge numerals must be quoted verbatim from the bound evidence document so the value is checkable against its source.

narration.description: Audio is the render clock. Beat times below are validated against these word timings; captions are derived, never hand-timed.

world.description: Resolved from the tagged plate catalogue. Never a sentence-native name.

ken_burns.description: One continuous move per scene. Vector and amplitude MUST differ between adjacent scenes; uniform ken burns reads as drift, not direction (doc 29 §1.4).

exit.description: Semantic transition palette. Always fires on an evidence-free boundary: docks clear first (doc 29 Part 6).

at.description: Seconds from episode start. Must fall on a word boundary in words_path.

caption.description: Spoken line for this beat. Keywords wrapped in {{ }} render in the accent color.

badges.description: Four-slot visibility mask: dock1.a, dock1.b, dock2.a, dock2.b. 'X' lit, '-' hidden. Badges only reveal, never retract within a scene.

oneOf.description: Dock is empty at this beat.
Key into the evidence table below.

title.description: Operator-written dock title. Not a claim; a handle.

document.description: The literal teacher-stamped slide. Rendered fully opaque — literal evidence is never translucent, only the dock chrome is (doc 29 §8.3).

crop.description: Optional source-bound crop. Must not clip the teacher stamp.

source.description: Provenance line shown in the citation footer.

badge.description: Code-drawn stat pill. The value is authored in code so it is exact by construction (generated imagery may not carry numerals — finance style profile generated_text_rule).

verbatim_in_document.description: Assertion that `value` appears verbatim in the bound document. The validator OCRs the slide and fails the build when it does not — this is what makes the evidence layer mechanically checkable rather than merely plausible.
